_william.pearson_: Nobody asked Oskar Pearson why he came. Nobody in S-F10 asks that. He was handed a spade before he was handed a rifle.
Oskar Pearson was in the first hundred. The old hands in S-F10 call them 'the early birds', and not always kindly.
On Day 3, Verdel Ridge passed to the Concord. Oskar Pearson wrote the name in his diary with unusual care.
Oskar Pearson found a shirt button in the bread. He ate around it and kept the button. Both were useful.
Oskar Pearson fired at a movement across the wire at S-F10. The man went down: Norbert Fransinlak, grazed.
valiantlyvaliancy: Nobody saw Otto Valiantlyval arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in S-F6, and a quiet sniper under it.

Otto Valiantlyval pulled Lucien Raphoto out of a flooded shell hole at the Brickworks. Neither of them has mentioned it since. Both of them remember. Day 3. The Concord took Verdel Ridge. From the heights Otto Valiantlyval could see the whole Hegemony line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.
Otto Valiantlyval noticed a loophole that had been dark for days. He watched it until dusk and wrote down what changed.

A clear shot from S-F6. Otto Valiantlyval badly wounded Yann Jimmysparrow and slid back down below the parapet. A letter from home reached Otto Valiantlyval before dusk. Otto Valiantlyval read it twice and slept a little easier.
wiwiwib3: Oskar "Whistle" Wiwiwib arrived with the Day 4 draft, carrying a pack of cards missing the queen of hearts and the news from home, which was old by the time he told it.
A parcel from home held a comb. Oskar "Whistle" Wiwiwib has hardly any hair left after the last haircut, but he appreciated the thought.
